problem_motivation.content: A need exists for cost-effective methods to incorporate high-entropy alloys with superior properties into harsh environments.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Development of high-entropy alloy (HEA) films is a promising and cost-effective way to incorporate these materials of superior properties in harsh environments.

problem_motivation.content: The high cost of metal powders required for bulk high-entropy alloys hinders their commercialization.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: the cost of metal powders used to develop bulk HEAs can hinder their commercialization as an alternative to the alloys in use.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies used cosputtering from multiple elemental targets to create RHEA films.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In contrast, Zou et al. reported an average grain size of 150 nm for a cosputtered RHEA film using elemental targets.

prior_approach.content: Feng et al. and Kim et al. reported grain sizes of 10 nm and 15.8 nm for RHEA films made using a high-entropy single target.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Similar low grain sizes have been reported for RHEA films developed using a high-entropy single target, e.g., Feng et al. and Kim et al. reported average grain sizes of 10 and 15.8 nm, respectively.

prior_limitation.content: There is a scarcity of reports on microstructural control to enhance the hardness, strength, and tribological performance of RHEA films.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, reports on microstructural control to enhance the hardness, strength, and tribological performance of RHEA films are scarce.

prior_limitation.content: Gallium ions from focused ion beam milling can significantly modify material mechanical properties by introducing defects and amorphizing the crystal structure.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: It has been shown that gallium ions can significantly modify the mechanical properties of the materials due to the introduction of defects and amorphization of the crystal structure.

prior_limitation.content: Cosputtering from multiple targets suffers from non-homogeneous atom distribution leading to weak sluggish diffusion and larger grains.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: This large difference in the grain size can be due to cosputtering from multiple targets, where sluggish diffusion is weak due to the nonhomogeneous distribution of atoms.

inspiration_source.content: The choice of RHEA composition was based on thermocalc simulations from previous work by the authors.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The RHEA composition has been chosen based on thermocalc simulation to obtain a mixture of a ductile FCC phase and a high-strength BCC solid solution, as reported in our previous work.

causal_claim.content: The nanocrystalline structure of the film caused an increase in hardness to 19 ± 2.3 GPa and elastic modulus to 259 ± 19.2 GPa.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.

causal_claim.content: Solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening resulted in a high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa was obtained in nanopillar compression due to solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening.

causal_claim.content: Annealing improves adhesion and stability, which is beneficial for tribological applications.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The enhanced adhesion and stability of the film after annealing can be found to be beneficial for tribological applications.

causal_claim.content: The addition of Cu increases hardness and nanopillar compressional strength compared to other RHEA films.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The use of Cu in RHEA films has been found to increase the hardness and nanopillar compressional strength compared to previously reported works on RHEA films.

mechanism_principle.content: The reduced lattice constant is attributed to the smaller atomic radius of Cu compared to other refractory atoms.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The reduced lattice constant can be related to the presence of Cu atoms having a smaller atomic radius than those of the other refractory atoms, which will reduce the lattice parameter.

mechanism_principle.content: The formation of nanocrystalline grains is attributed to high lattice distortion hindering island growth via sluggish diffusion.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: However, due to the presence of a high amount of distortion, the island growth is hindered by sluggish diffusion, one of the prime characteristics of high-entropy alloys, and leads to the formation of nanocrystalline grains.

mechanism_principle.content: Low Cu content is attributed to high sputtering rates of refractory elements causing Cu scattering.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The low amount of Cu can be related to the high sputtering of refractory elements, which could have resulted in more scattering of Cu atoms in the sputtering plasma after initial deposition.

mechanism_principle.content: High hardness is attributed to enhanced grain boundary strengthening from nanocrystallinity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: High hardness in a metallic film can be related to the enhanced grain boundary strengthening from nanocrystallinity.

mechanism_principle.content: Dislocation movement is hindered within columnar grains due to the (110) plane dominance and low diffusivity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The deposited RHEA film dominates in the (110) plane due to its relatively low diffusivity with increasing film thickness as compared to the (200) and (211) planes resulting in nanocrystalline grains.

mechanism_principle.content: The high compressional strength is attributed to solid solution hardening, grain size, and grain boundary strengthening.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The extremely high compressional strength of the BCC HEA nanopillar has been attributed to the combined effect of a substantial solid solution hardening effect, grain size, and grain boundary strengthening.

mechanism_principle.content: Strengthening shifts to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation due to the highly columnar structure, leading to intergranular fracture.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Furthermore, the higher strength of the nanocrystalline RHEA CuMoTaWV film arises due to the highly columnar structure of grains in the (110) direction. Thus, the strengthening mechanism in nanopillar HEAs shifts from dislocation-controlled to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation, which eventually leads to intergranular fracture.

mechanism_principle.content: Annealing improves adhesion and roughness through grain refinement.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: However, annealing the CuMoTaWV RHEA film at 300 °C improved the surface roughness through grain refinement and increased the adhesion of the film to the steel substrate, resulting in a steady-state average COF of 0.25

mechanism_principle.content: High friction at 300°C is attributed to tribochemical reactions forming oxides on the counterball.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The high COF at 300 °C relates to the tribochemical reaction of the RHEA film with the steel counterball, where the formation of oxides on the steel counterball can bias the frictional behavior.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study aims to investigate the effect of lattice distortion when combining Cu with refractory elements on mechanical properties and the enhancement of tribological properties via CuO formation.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The addition of Cu to the refractory elements MoTaWV was done to investigate (I) the effect of lattice distortion in the films on combining Cu with refractory elements and its contribution toward the mechanical properties, and (II) the enhancement of the tribological properties of the refractory high-entropy film at RT and moderate temperatures by lowering the friction coefficient and wear rate with the formation of CuO.

evidence_result.content: The RHEA film exhibited a coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.25 at room temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the RHEA film showed an average coefficient of friction (COF) and wear rate of 0.25 (RT)

evidence_result.content: The RHEA film exhibited a wear rate of 6.4 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/N m at room temperature.
The RHEA film had a COF 2 times lower than 304 stainless steel at room temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The COF was found to be 2 times lower at RT

evidence_result.content: The RHEA film had a wear rate 100 times lower than 304 stainless steel at room temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: and wear rate 10 2 times lower at RT

constraint.content: The maximum force applied during the microcompression tests of the nanopillars was set to 3 mN.
constraint.evidence_span: The pillars were then microcompressed using an Anton Paar ultra-nanoindentation tester in load control mode with the maximum force set to 3 mN.
